text: I'll start by looking at the workspace layout and searching for the receipt and discount code.
`build_discount_receipt` has a mutable default argument `lines: list[str] = []`, which would accumulate lines across calls — exactly the symptom. Let me read the file to confirm.

Confirmed: the default `lines` list is created once at function definition and shared across all calls with no `lines` argument, so every receipt keeps appending to the previous ones. I'll fix it with the standard `None` sentinel.
All 29 tests pass, including the leak test.

args.summary: Root cause: `build_discount_receipt` in library/discounts.py used a mutable default argument (`lines: list[str] = []`). That list is created once at import time and shared by every call that doesn't pass `lines`, so discount lines accumulated across orders for the life of the process. This explains both the unrelated `SAVE10` on a customer's receipt and why restarting the service "fixed" it. The fix changes the default to `None` and creates a fresh list inside the function when none is supplied. The full test suite passes (29/29), including the existing no-leak test.
